items.title: NASA Mars Analog Crew Completes 378-Day Isolation

items.summary: At the 10th German-Chinese Automotive Congress in Wolfsburg on October 30, 2026, about 600 representatives from China and Germany gathered to explore closer collaboration amid industry transformation. Officials described electrification, digitalization, artificial intelligence and autonomous driving as key drivers of change. Olaf Lies called the congress a strong signal for deeper cooperation; Thomas Schmall stressed maintaining dialogue between German and Chinese firms; Liu Minqiang said competition can help upgrade the sector. Hunan Province pitched its '5C' advantages to attract German investment, with Sany Group among companies present. The event coincided with the International Suppliers Fair.
items.title: Chinese and German auto firms deepen cooperation at Wolfsburg congress

items.summary: Chen Yuwen, a researcher at the International Cooperation Center of the National Development and Reform Commission, outlines how Chinese private enterprises support high-quality economic development. A November 1, 2018 symposium set six policy measures to ease tax burdens, financing difficulties and costs while protecting entrepreneurs' safety and property. The article notes that by end of April 2026, private firms in the 'four new' sectors reached 24.619 million (40.3% of all private enterprises), per SAMR data. In foreign trade, their share rose from 39.7% in 2018 to 57.3% in 2025, and they provide over 80% of urban employment. The Private Economy Promotion Law took effect on May 20, 2025, reinforcing equal treatment and fair competition.
items.title: Chinese Private Enterprises Drive High-Quality Economic Growth

items.summary: The 2026 Light of the Internet Expo opened Monday in Wuzhen, Zhejiang Province, as a flagship event of the World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit. It showcased more than 1,000 new technologies and products from 671 companies across 54 countries, plus over 100 embodied intelligent robots for sectors such as manufacturing, healthcare and elderly care.
items.title: Satellite Internet, 6G and Robots Shine at Wuzhen Expo

items.summary: The Supreme Court of India responded sharply on Monday to a plea about steep airfare increases. Justice Vikram Nath told the counsel, "Don't travel by air," before moving on. The court did not take up the plea at that stage and proceeded to the next matter.
items.title: Supreme Court Judge Dismisses Plea Over Airfare Hike

items.summary: The BJP alleged a rift in Congress leadership, claiming Rahul Gandhi's camp was sidelining his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra ahead of the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. Spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said she was denied speaking opportunities and seated second row during events on October 31. He offered no independent evidence to support these claims.
items.title: BJP Alleges Rift Between Gandhi Siblings Over Ramlila Rally Role

items.summary: The Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission approved tariffs discovered through competitive bidding for a 450 MW / 900 MWh standalone battery storage project in Gujarat. Allocated to NLC India Renewables Limited and Sun Drops Energia Limited under GUVNL's Phase-IX procurement, the projects follow an earlier developer failure to execute agreements. Supported by Viability Gap Funding, they aim to meet Energy Storage Obligations while strengthening grid stability.
items.title: GERC Approves Tariffs for Gujarat Battery Storage Projects

items.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier visited China in October, arriving on the 27th before talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping that began around October 30. In Hefei he toured Volkswagen's largest research center outside Germany, where technologies were developed by a local joint venture for China's smart-auto market. Both leaders framed the trip as evidence of a shift from trade-focused ties toward innovation partnerships in artificial intelligence and green development. Steinmeier said dialogue could resolve trade differences while supporting free-trade rules; Xi called for cooperation based on equality and mutual benefit, describing it as an engine for broader China-EU relations.
items.title: China and Germany Chart Deeper Innovation Partnership

items.summary: Andy Burnham declined in an ITV interview to say net migration was too high, though he said small boat crossings were 'too high, for certain'. Shabana Mahmood will later announce tougher indefinite leave to remain rules requiring longer waits. The context has shifted as net migration falls and Reform UK's poll lead recedes.
items.title: Burnham declines net migration claim as Mahmood prepares settlement rules

items.summary: John Leeson, best known as the voice of the robot dog K9 in Doctor Who, has died at 83. His son Guy Ducker announced it after a summer of illness, describing an end that was peaceful. Colleagues remembered him for his distinctive performance and his work across stage, television and audio dramas.
items.title: John Leeson, voice of K9 in Doctor Who, dies aged 83

items.summary: A business jet crashed into a multi-lane road near Cresthaven, Palm Beach County, Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people aboard. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the deaths and said the FAA was assisting an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Board. Governor Ron DeSantis called the scene jarring, describing it as a missile coming down with a massive explosion.
items.title: Nine Killed When Business Jet Crashes Into Florida Street

items.summary: Ryanair is considering cost-cutting measures, including temporary pay freezes, lower crew ratios and greater use of AI, to offset soaring jet-fuel costs driven by the Middle East conflict. Its own fuel bill could rise by about €2bn in its next financial year, ending March 2028. Chief executive Michael O’Leary said fares may increase materially but would not fully cover higher prices.
items.title: Ryanair weighs pay freezes and crew cuts as fuel costs surge

items.summary: Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff as it copes with sharply higher fuel costs driven by the US-Israel war with Iran. The carrier forecasts its short-term fuel bill to rise €2bn (£1.6bn) and says European airfares will increase, though it doubts that alone will cover bills. Pre-tax profits fell 16% to €2.4bn in the six months to end of September. CEO Michael O'Leary expects fares up 15% to 20% next year but warns they may not offset rising oil costs.
items.title: Ryanair weighs pay freeze and fare hikes over fuel surge

items.summary: Two days before Michigan’s midterm legislative elections, Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens endorsed her progressive rival Abdul El‑Sayed’s opponent, Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers. The move followed a dispute in which El‑Sayed said Stevens was no longer welcome at his campaign events and that she should “away.” Stevens posted the endorsement on X on November 1, 2026, after appearing with Mr. Rogers at a Detroit church event. U.S. President Donald Trump praised her decision as “bravery,” while several of her congressional office staffers resigned in response. El‑Sayed dismissed the drama, saying it did not matter to him.
items.title: Michigan Democrat Endorses Republican Rival Amid Party Rift

items.summary: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) published a list identifying press freedom 'predators' for an interview marking the United Nations International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists. Thibaut Bruttin, RSF's Director General and Secretary-General, welcomed the occasion, stating that when journalists are killed it is everyone's right to know what is being endangered.
items.title: RSF Releases List of Press Freedom Predators Ahead of UN Day

items.summary: An EL PAÍS USA Edition article frames the upcoming November 3 U.S. midterm election as a referendum on whether Trumpism survives, describing Donald Trump's record-setting campaign tour dubbed 'Midterm Blitz,' which will have brought him to 28 rallies and about 60 hours of events by Election Day. The piece notes that Republicans trailed eight points in generic ballot polling before the summer and may lose the House while ceding the Senate remains a remote prospect. It presents early voting figures — just over 51 million citizens as of Saturday, which forecast high turnout — with two readings offered: one favoring Republican mobilization, another bolstering Democratic hopes. The article also examines Elon Musk's spending at least $267 million to support Republicans in the midterms compared with roughly $290 million for Trump's 2024 campaign, and notes his fortune grew by about $2.7 billion since returning to power.
items.title: Trump's Midterm Blitz Framed as a Referendum on Trumpism

items.summary: More companies in Japan are taking out cybersecurity insurance policies following several high-profile data breaches, including last week's attack on GMO Internet Group. Such incidents highlight the significant financial risk that cyberattacks pose to businesses. The coverage typically includes compensation for breach-related costs such as hacking and internal leaks, digital forensic analysis to identify attackers and system vulnerabilities, prevention assessments, and losses from missed business opportunities.
items.title: Japanese firms increase cybersecurity insurance after data breaches

items.summary: The U.N.'s peacekeeping mission for disputed Western Sahara, MINURSO, ceased operations on Sunday after 35 years amid a U.S.-Russia standoff over the territory's future. The secretary-general announced that 1 November 2026 marks the start of the liquidation period, with a smaller team overseeing asset disposal. Russia vetoed a draft resolution supporting Morocco and ended the mission next year; a rival Russian extension vote was also defeated. Morocco welcomed the non-renewal as an instrument to internationalize the dispute, while Algeria-backed Polisario called it unacceptable. The force had been authorized for 534 personnel with a budget of more than $62 million in 2026-2027.
items.title: UN Peacekeeping Mission in Western Sahara Ends After 35 Years

items.summary: The Bank of Japan said a shrinking population makes robust consumer-spending growth unlikely, warning weak aggregate consumption may not signal weaker household demand. The internal affairs ministry reported a 2.5% fall in 2025, the fastest since 1920. BNP Paribas and Daiichi Life Research Institute forecast Q3 GDP decline due Nov. 16.
items.title: Bank of Japan Cautions on Consumer Spending Amid Population Decline

items.summary: Micron Technology gave Boise $2.5 million in December to extend its geothermal heating system, the country’s largest, toward a planned affordable housing development with more than 300 units. The city says renewable heat could save residents up to 80% on utility bills and support Boise’s goal of becoming carbon-neutral by 2050.
items.title: Boise Expands Geothermal Network With Micron Funding

items.summary: Exclusive Grist polling from Data for Progress shows that about 58 percent of likely U.S. voters believe a warming climate will hinder their ability to achieve or maintain the American Dream over the next 20 years, including 42 percent of Republicans. The survey was conducted this spring with 1,167 likely voters and found cost of living as the top current threat, while only about 2 percent named climate change first. Grace Adcox of Data for Progress noted that voters may resist sacrifice framing despite Trump’s rhetoric linking his policies to the American Dream.
items.title: Poll Finds Voters See Climate Change as Threat to American Dream

items.summary: The Communist Party of China concluded its fifth plenary session in Beijing, adopting a resolution titled Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. The resolution stressed maintaining a tough stance against corruption and strengthening checks on power.
items.title: China's CPC Concludes Fifth Plenary Session on Party Self-Governance

items.summary: Kylian Mbappé apologised after a meme depicting him as Chinese leader Mao Zedong drew backlash in China. In a video, he said his favourite meme showed 'a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator', before an altered image placed his face on Mao's body. At least three Chinese companies ended brand deals with him, and CCTV pulled a Real Madrid match from its schedule.
items.title: Mbappé Apologises After Mao Meme Comment Sparks Chinese Backlash

items.summary: Germany's digital minister Karsten Wildberger confirmed that members of the Bundestag and federal government received warnings from Apple that their iPhones may have been targeted by mercenary spyware. The alerts began reaching affected phones on 29 October, per a Federal Office for Information Security letter seen by Wildberger. Those affected were told to treat their devices as compromised, though it remains unknown who is behind the attack or how many people were hit.
items.title: German officials warned iPhones targeted by spyware

items.summary: Pakistan’s Private Power and Infrastructure Board is seeking a consultant to support the development of 100 MW of distributed solar power plants in Gilgit-Baltistan. The Water and Power Department will execute the project, while the chosen consultant verifies non-solar works such as transmission lines and substations. Applications open with an expression of interest stage and are due November 30; international bidders may apply.
items.title: Pakistan Board Seeks Consultant for Distributed Solar Project

items.summary: A Brookings Institution report says the Department of Government Efficiency removed about $468 million from tribal programs, roughly half for environmental and natural resources. The cuts follow a 2025 cancellation by the Trump administration of an EPA wind-energy grant to Kotzebue, Alaska, that would have cut diesel reliance toward 40–50 percent. Brookings links the losses to One Big Beautiful Bill Act repeals of Inflation Reduction Act streams and flags historic Biden-era tribal funding at over $700 million as now defunded. Authors Rob Maxim and Glencora Haskins call for Congress to bar grant cancellation and route funds directly to tribes, citing trust obligations amid worsening climate disasters.
items.title: DOGE Cuts $468M in Tribal Climate Funding

items.summary: A one-year-old child died in a house fire in Western Australia's South West, with authorities investigating the cause. Firefighters extinguished the blaze at a home in Collie, about 200 kilometres south of Perth, on Sunday afternoon before the body was found. Police said several people were inside but escaped safely. A WA Police spokesperson said the death is not being treated as suspicious and that a coroner's report would be prepared.
items.title: One-Year-Old Dies in House Fire Near Perth

items.summary: Charities giving Christmas presents to struggling families say more children need help but donations are falling this year. Martyna Lee, founder of the Chard appeal started in 2019 from her living room, said families worry about affording gifts and have 'tears in their eyes'. She noted they receive more referrals and fewer donations due to cost of living. Gill Harrison of Christmas Sparkle in Taunton reported demand rising sharply over recent years - from 500 presents given out in 2015 to around 10,000 individual gifts last year - with possibly higher requests expected this year as the cost-of-living crisis continues.
items.title: Somerset charities report rising Christmas gift demand amid cost of living crisis

items.summary: A recent study confirms that the Bangka slow loris, declared possibly extinct on the IUCN Red List in 2015 after its last documented sighting around 1937, still survives. Researchers analyzed more than 90 lorises rescued by Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center and mapped 39 across four districts of Bangka Island in 2021, indicating wide distribution. Co-author Timon Glaw noted the species had been overlooked for nearly a century. The authors state it is not yet extinct and recommend reassessment, habitat protections, post-release tracking, and an ex-situ breeding program.
items.title: Rescued Primate Confirms Survival of Species Once Listed as Possibly Extinct

items.summary: A private Learjet 60 crashed Sunday in Cresthaven, Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people aboard after nose-diving into a residential area and exploding. Air traffic control recordings show the pilots reporting turbulence, icing and precipitation before descent accelerated to up to 30,000 feet per minute — exceeding design limits. The National Transportation Safety Board has launched an investigation; cause and identities remain unknown.
items.title: Nine Killed When Learjet Crashes in South Florida Neighborhood

items.summary: The Geelong Cats finished second on percentage behind North Melbourne after becoming the highest-scoring regular-season AFLW team of all time, with a final score of 88 to 20. Co-captain Nina Morrison said their rise to premiership contenders “doesn't feel like it's come out of the blue.” The Cats face Melbourne in Saturday's qualifying final at Princes Park.
items.title: Geelong Cats surge into AFLW finals contention

items.summary: Friends and family mourn the death of TV actor Anuj Thakur, who died last week after a seizure during sleep. Casting director Rupesh Sonar shared tributes on Instagram, saying he had met Thakur just ten days earlier.
items.title: TV Actor Anuj Thakur Dies at 33 After Seizure in Sleep

items.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of forcibly shutting shops in Connaught Place on 1 November, ahead of the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan. In a video shared on his social media account, he said traders had been told to shop during the march but found every single shop closed. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh later called fears about trader losses a smear campaign and thanked Delhi's business community for supporting the protest. Chamber of Trade & Industry chairman Brijesh Goyal estimated trading-sector losses at ₹10,000–11,000 crore, citing updates from traders' WhatsApp groups that said around 80% of shops stayed closed. BJP leaders, including JP Nadda and Amit Shah, echoed the concerns while criticising Congress for ignoring postponement requests during the festive season.
items.title: BJP Blamed for Delhi Shop Closures as Traders Warn of Festive Losses

items.summary: A retractable solar roof of 5,280 photovoltaic modules is under construction above the aeration tanks at Stuttgart-Mühlhausen’s main wastewater treatment plant. Stadtwerke Stuttgart says it will reach an installed capacity of 2.745 MW on completion in the second quarter of 2027, making it Germany’s largest retractable solar roof. The project uses Helioflex technology from dhp Technology and is expected to generate more than 2.2 GWh annually for on-site use.
items.title: Stuttgart Builds Germany’s Largest Retractable Solar Roof Over Wastewater Plant

items.summary: Senior Delhi journalist Ajaz Ashraf argues that Congress should boycott the February-MMarch 2027 State Assembly elections to pressure the Modi government into electoral reforms. Writing about Rahul Gandhi’s INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, where speakers targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, he frames a boycott as a principled stand rather than a gamble tied to election outcomes. Ashraf contends Congress alone has an all-India footprint and can bear the cost—Uttarakhand, Punjab and Goa together account for just 20 Lok Sabha seats—drawing on historical precedents from 1937. He warns that winning could let BJP claim electoral fairness while losing would stall reforms.
items.title: Congress Should Boycott Assembly Elections To Defend Democracy

items.summary: M K Stalin and Thangam Thennarasu accused the ruling TVK government of driving Tamil Nadu into an economic downturn. Stalin cited GST revenue growth falling below India's national average of 22.9 per cent in October, plus a reported Rs 1,614-crore Korean investment proposal relocating to Andhra Pradesh. Thennarasu said Tamil Nadu's collections grew only 3 per cent versus 24 per cent for Andhra Pradesh, and contracted by 1 per cent in August and 5 per cent in September. Both leaders called on the government to boost domestic production.
items.title: DMK leaders blame Vijay government for Tamil Nadu's economic slowdown

items.summary: The Supreme Court refused urgent listing of a plea alleging nearly a 700 per cent rise in airfares, telling a petitioner on Monday not to travel by air. An advocate claimed fares had jumped that much and called aviation an essential service violating Article 14. The court is separately hearing S Laxminarayanan's petition for a robust regulator; the Centre said rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 are likely to be published soon. The article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.
items.title: Supreme Court Tells Petitioner Not To Travel By Air Amid Fare Hike Plea

items.summary: Hidden-camera footage shows Punjab Police ASI Sukhdev Singh placing heroin under a mattress at Shiv Sena leader Mahant Kashmir Giri's Khanna residence. A police team then recovered around 30 grams of the drug, and Giri was arrested before being discharged from the case. The video prompted his suspension, an SIT probe, and political backlash as Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal attacked the AAP government.
items.title: Punjab cop caught planting drugs at Sena leader's home

items.summary: Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara says Virat Kohli has a better chance than opener Rohit Sharma of scoring a century in the upcoming five-match ODI series against New Zealand. He attributes this to Kohli’s number-three position, which suits an anchor role and gives him time to settle. Pujara also expects the series to be closely contested.
items.title: Kohli has better chance of scoring century than Rohit: Pujara drops big verdict

items.summary: Europe is preparing a digital battery passport required for e-bike batteries sold in the EU from February 18, 2027. The rule stems from the EU’s 2023 Batteries Regulation and covers cars, bicycles, scooters and other light electric vehicles. Scanning QR codes may reveal manufacturer, chemistry, capacity and carbon data, though some details could stay restricted to authorized users. Because many manufacturers sell in both regions, US riders might eventually benefit through spillover rather than a new American law.
items.title: EU Battery Passport May Reach US E-Bike Riders

items.summary: Author Parvathi Sajiv presents a book tracing Indian protest history from the freedom struggle through movements to the early 2020s, examining how they shaped laws and public discourse. She notes many protests took decades before prompting government action. Citing the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, she reports 110 anti-government protests worldwide in the last twelve months, with 31 active as of July 29, 2026, attributing them to governments’ anti-democratic actions. The book highlights India’s current resistance to the ₹44,000-crore Ken-Betwa Link Project and concludes that satyagraha remains a unifying thread in Indian protest. Excerpted with permission from Duckbill Publishing.
items.title: New Book Explores How Protests Shaped Laws in India

items.summary: Three Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLAs from Punjab joined the Bharatiya Janata Party on Monday, ahead of Assembly elections expected early next year. Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jauramajra resigned Sunday; Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh followed that day. BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon called the AAP a “sinking ship” and said more resignations were expected, while AAP chief Aman Arora accused the BJP of gathering expelled leaders with no base in Punjab.
items.title: Three AAP MLAs Join BJP Ahead of Punjab Assembly Polls

items.summary: Turkish firm TAV Airports announced a second-phase investment of $353.9 million at Almaty Airport, raising its total in Kazakhstan to around $642.5 million. CEO Serkan Kaptan said the initial program completed in 2024 delivered new terminals. The airport nearly doubled passenger traffic to 11.9 million by 2025 and handled 9.47 million passengers through September this year, with international arrivals up 11%. TAV has operated it since 2021.
items.title: TAV Airports Expands Almaty Airport Investment Amid Türkiye-Kazakhstan Ties

items.summary: Vedanta Oil and Gas shares rose to Rs 31.90 on Monday, part of a two-day rally after the company reported consolidated net profit of Rs 746 crore for the second quarter of FY27, up from a Rs 91 crore loss a year earlier but down from Rs 945 crore in the first quarter. Revenue rose over 6% to Rs 2,488 crore and EBITDA jumped 34% YoY to Rs 1,393 crore.
items.title: Vedanta Oil and Gas Shares Jump After Q2 Profit

items.summary: Police say eight to ten men allegedly tampered with railway signalling to halt the Mumbai-Kolhapur Mahalaxmi Express in Satara district, Maharashtra, and robbed three women passengers of gold ornaments worth around ₹2 lakh. The incident occurred near Salpa railway station around 2.30am on Sunday. Investigators are conducting a search operation while questions arise about security arrangements despite RPF presence.
items.title: Maharashtra Gang Robs Women Passengers of Gold on Trained Train

items.summary: GAIL reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 4,719.66 crore in Q2FY27, up 139.3% year-on-year to Rs 4,720 crore, with revenue from operations rising 32.7% YoY to Rs 47,301.03 crore. The company's board approved an initial public offering for its wholly owned subsidiary GAIL Gas Ltd, involving dilution of up to 25% of GAIL's equity stake, and cleared the transfer of six city gas distribution areas—Varanasi, Patna, Ranchi, East Singhbhum, Cuttack and Khordha—to that subsidiary. Shares gained about 4% on the results.
items.title: GAIL Shares Rise on Strong Q2 Profit and GAIL Gas IPO Approval

items.summary: On Monday, Russia and Ukraine exchanged accusations over cyberattacks on their emergency alert systems. Moscow reported a hack of its emergency alerts app hours after Kyiv said its own air raid warning system had been compromised. The incidents coincided with the expiry of a fragile ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region, raising fears of renewed fighting.
items.title: Russia and Ukraine Trade Cyberattack Blame as Ceasefire Ends

items.summary: A few dozen right-wing activists gathered outside Gadi Eisenkot's residence in Herzliya to oppose the new Israeli-Arab coalition. Protester Viktor Shriki said the demonstration aimed to block a Palestinian state formed with Arab and Muslim groups. Netanyahu warned against what he called a dangerous government, noting Arab parties represent 20% of Israel's population, while Likud claimed Tuesday's election was stolen without providing evidence.
items.title: Right-wing activists protest Israeli-Arab coalition government plans
